key_insight: The paper shows that fracture in highly deformable thin structures must be modeled together with large geometric changes, and it does so with a unified discrete differential geometry phase-field framework.
engineering_relevance: The method helps design flexible, damage-tolerant thin structures such as flexible electronics by predicting how cracks, bending, snapping, and reconfiguration interact during loading.
method: Discrete differential geometry on a triangulated midsurface for membrane and bending elasticity
Phase field defined on the same surface to track crack initiation and growth
Staggered solve with active-set irreversibility plus degradation-deletion for full crack opening
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite element results in 2D and successful 3D tearing simulations that reproduce crack convergence, coalescence, snap-through, and island--bridge behavior.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion and topology reconstruction steps may add implementation complexity and could be sensitive to mesh quality and parameter choices.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
